summary: Feed s129_double to NDR is degraded: 98.9% encrypted traffic exceeds 90% tolerance and 60.1% of frames are ERSPAN-encapsulated, both blinding payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Nearly all bytes (98.86%) are TLS/encrypted and delivered without decryption; NDR is receiving opaque payloads because no SSL visibility/decryption zone is configured before the packet broker egress.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection and tolerates ~90% encrypted; at 99% encrypted it cannot perform deep packet inspection, JA3, or payload analytics, severely reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt or selectively forward decrypted traffic from a trusted decryption device so NDR receives cleartext payload it can analyze; alternatively filter to focus NDR on decryptable/cleartext segments.

findings.root_cause: 60.1% of frames (1218/2027) arrive inside ERSPAN tunnel; packet broker is forwarding encapsulated traffic from remote ERSPAN source without stripping the outer header before delivery to tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees outer ERSPAN headers instead of inner original flows, failing to parse inner IP/TCP and application payload, causing missed detections and broken flow reassembly despite needing full payload and both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip ERSPAN encapsulation and deliver inner original packets so NDR can correctly decode flows and inspect payload.
